members: [untitled BTM module] These genes mark the erythroid-megakaryocytic branch of hematopoiesis, the programme by which bone marrow progenitors commit to making red cells and platelets rather than lymphoid or granulocytic fates. Its transcriptional core is a TAL1-GFI1B axis that drives erythroid gene expression while restraining progenitor proliferation; loss of either blocks red cell production, and GFI1B mutation causes a bleeding disorder with malformed platelets.

[untitled BTM module] These genes outline the terminal stages of erythroid differentiation, in which a committed progenitor remodels its membrane and cytoskeleton, condenses and expels its nucleus, and emerges as a deformable red cell able to survive repeated passage through capillaries and the spleen. Structural components dominate: beta-spectrin builds the membrane skeleton beneath the lipid bilayer, pleckstrin-2 and cortactin drive the actin rearrangements required for enucleation and cell shaping, and XK forms a disulphide-linked complex with the Kell glycoprotein at the erythrocyte surface.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on stress-activated transcriptional signalling and its supporting membrane and metabolic machinery. Its recognisable core is the kinase TAK1 (MAP3K7) acting upstream of the CREB/ATF family factors ATF1 and ATF2, a route by which cytokine, TGF-beta and stress inputs are converted into changes in gene expression governing inflammation, survival and differentiation; loss of TAK1 signalling causes inflammatory and developmental failure.

[untitled BTM module] The genes here sketch late erythroid differentiation and the assembly of the red cell surface. Erythropoiesis matters because it supplies the circulating oxygen carriers, and its transcriptional and membrane components determine both red cell mechanical resilience and the antigens that decide transfusion compatibility.
name_1: Erythroid commitment and terminal red cell differentiation
name_2: Transcriptional control of erythroid differentiation and red cell maturation

[untitled BTM module] These genes converge on the braking and tuning of growth-factor signalling as it feeds into transcription, a control layer whose loss produces overgrowth, cancer and neurodevelopmental disease. Two GTPase-activating proteins, RASA2 for Ras and ACAP2 for an Arf-family GTPase, terminate signalling at the membrane, while MAP3K2 relays kinase input downstream and sorting nexins SNX13 and SNX14 govern endosomal trafficking and receptor fate.

[untitled BTM module] These genes converge on nuclear organisation and nucleocytoplasmic traffic: chromatin architecture, mRNA processing, ribosome biogenesis and export of cargo through the nuclear pore. CTCF and the cohesin subunit SMC1A together define chromatin loop boundaries and insulate promoters from inappropriate enhancers, which is how genome folding is translated into transcriptional output; ADNP and ATF1 act on transcription, the latter as a CREB-family factor responding to cAMP signalling.

[untitled BTM module] These genes converge on the regulation of gene expression at the steps between transcription and protein turnover. Cyclin T2 partners CDK9 in the elongation kinase that releases paused RNA polymerase II, while cyclin C works within the Mediator kinase module that gates promoter engagement, and ARID4A and SP3 act on chromatin and promoter DNA to set which genes are read.

[untitled BTM module] These genes outline the myeloid identity and activation program of monocytes and macrophages, the cells that patrol tissue for microbes and debris and set the tone of an inflammatory response. The transcription factor SPI1 (PU.1) specifies this lineage together with HHEX, while TLR4 senses bacterial lipopolysaccharide and PTAFR responds to platelet-activating factor, coupling through the Src-family kinase LYN, the phospholipase PLCB2 and the ITAM-bearing adaptor TYROBP (DAP12) to calcium mobilization and cytoskeletal change; DOK2 acts as a brake on this kinase signaling.
